headline: Medium prompt-injection and data-leakage risk: Pipecat’s shared bus and broad egress can amplify Opik outputs into unsafe downstream use.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Pipecat documents a shared bus and multiple-instance shared state, so if Opik outputs are routed into that bus, instruction-like content can be replayed across sessions. Opik’s REST API and broad egress make it plausible it emits content that Pipecat may ingest. The exact bridge is undocumented, so uncertainty pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF Opik outputs are forwarded into Pipecat's shared bus
IF Pipecat parses upstream text as instructions or tool directives
mitigations: Add a one-line sanitizer that strips instruction markers before bus publish
Route Opik output through a read-only queue with provenance tags
Disable shared-bus fanout for untrusted transcripts
requires-engineering: add provenance-aware parsing and allowlists

B_data_leakage.rationale: Pipecat touches text, audio, video, images, and conversation state, and its docs list many third-party STT/LLM/TTS endpoints. Opik has broad network egress and REST API access, so if both share a workspace or transcript stream, sensitive conversation data can leave the pair through external APIs. The shared workspace is not proven, but the documented surfaces make leakage plausible in default deployments.
conditions: IF both agents process the same transcript or workspace artifacts
IF Pipecat is configured to use any third-party STT/LLM/TTS service
mitigations: Restrict Pipecat to local-only providers for a test run
Remove secrets and PII from shared transcripts before handoff
Turn off telemetry and analytics exports
requires-engineering: isolate workspaces per agent

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Pipecat explicitly supports multiple instances with shared bus state, while Opik exposes REST API egress. If both write to the same mutable resource or bus, concurrent updates can race or overwrite each other. No locking or coordination primitive is documented for the pair, so the overlap is real but not proven high-severity.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same shared bus or mutable transcript store
IF no external lock or version check is enabled
mitigations: Serialize writes through a single dispatcher
Use per-agent namespaces for bus topics
Add optimistic version checks on shared records
requires-engineering: introduce locking around shared state

D_cascading_error.rationale: Pipecat can consume many upstream services, and Opik can emit evaluation or observability outputs over REST. If Pipecat treats Opik-produced text as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream speech, video, or LLM actions. Because verification steps are not documented, the safer choice is medium rather than low.
conditions: IF Pipecat uses Opik output as an input prompt, transcript, or routing decision
IF no human or schema verification step is inserted
mitigations: Insert a schema validator before Pipecat consumes Opik output
Require human approval for action-bearing messages
Log and diff upstream outputs before execution
requires-engineering: add typed contracts between agents

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and no regulated data class or residency constraint is documented for Opik; Pipecat documents analytics and third-party service integrations, which can create policy mismatch if sensitive audio/text is routed externally. Because the compliance gap is not explicit in the profiles, this stays low.
conditions: IF regulated data is routed through Pipecat's external STT/LLM/TTS providers
IF the deployment requires residency or retention guarantees not configured here
mitigations: Disable external analytics and telemetry
Use only providers with matching residency terms
Document retention settings for transcripts
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for data routing
